imas_ambix/agent/llm_watch.py:499 document_engines reads the engines array the change populates

findings.text: A non-default pool spanning one engine is published by router.py:2555-2575 through build_lane_document plus _gate_fields, and neither sets engine_id, hostname or host (lane.py:854-1000 carries no such key). _document_engines returns that document as an engine entry anyway, so panel_engines emits it as a gate-only row with engine=None and host=None that can never satisfy the host test at live_panel.py:786, while the recorder's live row for the same engine is emitted separately with no gate: two rows for one engine, neither joined. Reproduced against the reviewed head with the module imported from a c96c1512 export: entry {'engine': '98dci4-gpu-0007', 'tok_s': 50.0, 'available': None, 'joined': False} plus entry {'engine': None, 'host': None, 'available': 93.0, 'joined': False}, two rows for one engine. The fragment's claim at watch-shows-several-engines.html:60-62 that a second model served by a single engine reaches the view is therefore not met, and the guard test hides it by hand-writing the engine_id at tests/test_live_panel.py:1026 that the router never writes.

test_a_second_models_pool_document_reaches_the_engine_list asserts an engine_id list built from a fixture whose lanes document carries "engine_id": "98dci4-gpu-0007:18811", a field the router's single-engine branch never sets (router.py:2555-2575 with lane.py:854-1000), so the assertion is true of a document shape production cannot produce and survives the very defect it was added to catch.

assert deepseek["running"] == pytest.approx(deepseek["live"]["mean_running"]) compares an entry field with the field _engine_entry copies it from (live_panel.py:849-861), so the two sides move together; it restates the passthrough instead of an independent measurement.

the panel_engines docstring states the join is by "engine identity -- the registration id's host and port", but _matching_engine (live_panel.py:786) compares the host and then the served model and never reads a port, and _pool_identity's port element (live_panel.py:805-815) is computed and never used; the documented identity is not the one implemented.

the gate log's revision header reads "# revision: 743e66db" while the tree it tested is the head c96c1512 -- the 102 collected items include the 8 tests that exist only at the head -- so a promotion gate comparing the recorded log revision against reviewed_head_sha reads a stale revision for a run that did test the head.

justifications.durability: the join has a real guard -- reverting it reddens test_two_serves_on_one_host_each_carry_their_own_figures per negative-control.log -- but test_a_second_models_pool_document_reaches_the_engine_list (tests/test_live_panel.py:1026) builds a document field the router never writes, so it cannot fail for the defect it claims to cover.
justifications.evidence: gate.log records 102 passed with a bare EXIT=0 and negative-control.log holds EXIT=1 with tests/test_live_panel.py::test_two_serves_on_one_host_each_carry_their_own_figures among the failing ids, though the gate log's revision header names 743e66db rather than the head.
justifications.fit: the helpers follow the module's own idiom, but live_panel.py:729 states the identity as host and port while the join at :786 compares host and model and _pool_identity's port element at :805 is never read.
justifications.goal_fidelity: live_panel.py:907 now joins by host and served model and reads every lanes-indexed pool, but a second model served by a single engine arrives as a duplicate identity-less row (live_panel.py:986), so that half of the claimed dimension is not delivered.
justifications.reuse: no other reader of the lanes index exists in imas_ambix at this revision; _lane_document (live_panel.py:925) extends the module that already owns the lane-document read rather than forking one.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff (live_panel.py, tests/test_live_panel.py, tests/test_llm_watch.py, the fragment) is inside the manifest's declared write paths.

verdicts.diff: Read commit by commit between 743e66db and c96c1512: one production commit (join and pool reading in live_panel.py), one tests commit adding 8 tests across the two test modules, and the fragment rewrite; no out-of-scope file is touched.
verdicts.done_when: The done_when names tests/test_llm_watch.py tests/test_lane_callers.py tests/test_live_panel.py with 102 collected items plus a whole-tree ruff check; gate.log records '102 passed in 1.15s' and EXIT=0 and ruff.log records the lint gate.
verdicts.goal: The node goal is one entry per engine from the pool documents and the per-engine live block; c96c1512 fixes the join at live_panel.py:762 to host+model and merges every pool document named by the lanes index at live_panel.py:943, which is what the review round asked for.
verdicts.manifest: The manifest reports four commits, 102 passed, ruff clean, and a negative control at negative-control.log; the control log holds EXIT=1 with two named failing ids, so the claim is backed by a file.
verdicts.write_paths: The four paths in 743e66db..c96c1512 -- imas_ambix/agent/live_panel.py, tests/test_live_panel.py, tests/test_llm_watch.py, docs/evidence/fragments/serving-across-servers/watch-shows-several-engines.html -- are all inside the declared write paths of the reviewed run.
